title: Policy heuristics for region/tier routing during staggered model rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As customers adopt model version pinning and phased rollouts (canary and A/B), we see complex interactions with region selection and customer tier routing. Current behavior can be surprising: a pinned version in eu-west may be bypassed by a tier-based route to 'low-latency' GPUs in us-east, or canaries that are only deployed in a single region can get uneven traffic when global traffic is routed by tier. This ticket defines product-level heuristics and policy defaults to ensure predictable, auditable routing in the presence of version pinning and staged rollouts.

Goals:
- Define a deterministic precedence order for routing rules (pinning, canary weights, region affinity, tier preferences).
- Surface policy behavior clearly in Console and APIs so customers can reason about outcomes and avoid accidental bypassing of pin/rollout intents.
- Provide fallback semantics when target variants are unavailable in the resolved region/tier.
- Minimize global customer impact and offer safe defaults for gradual rollouts across regions and dedicated vs hosted tiers.

Problem statement: Multiple overlapping policies (model version pin, per-route tier constraints, region overrides, canary weights) currently produce non-intuitive decisions during peak load and cross-region failover. Customers using private deployments with strict data residency rely on pinning to a specific model; if routing heuristics ignore explicit pin when honoring tier routing, this is unacceptable. Conversely, some customers expect canary traffic to follow the global canary weight independent of region, while others expect locality to be preserved. We need a policy that balances these needs and provides explicit knobs for customers to override defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document a precedence matrix: pinning > region affinity > customer-tier constraints > canary weight (configurable per project)
Console shows effective route resolution for a given request (region, tier, pin, canary percent) with an explainable reasoning trace
API accepts an explicit override flag (enforce_pin=true) that guarantees model pin enforcement even if it increases latency or violates tier constraints

Fallback policy documented: if pinned variant not available in resolved region, then: 1) if enforce_pin=true -> return 409 with diagnostic; 2) else -> fall back to nearest compatible variant (document search order) and log event
Integration tests that simulate cross-region traffic and tier capacity constraints validate the precedence matrix and fallback outcomes
Migration notes for existing customers and default behaviour changes (rolling opt-in) published in product annoucement
notes: Trade-offs considered: Enforcing pin always preserves correctness for data-residency but can increase latency or cost. Making canary global preserves experimentation signal across regions but risks violating locality constraints.
We should avoid introducing a new 'magic' priority that is invisible in Console — every default must be explainable and overrideable.
Eng should produce a simulation harness to show traffic allocation across regions for common rollout patterns (canary-only-in-region, weighted-A/B, phased-region-rollout).
tasks: Finalize precedence matrix and edge cases with Eng (deliverable: precedence_spec.md)
Design mockups for Console explain panel and API response fields (owner: Design)
Add API flag enforce_pin with clear error codes and auditing events (ENG work)
Build integration test scenarios and perf guardrails for fallback path
Prepare migration & customer communication plan (support playbook + FAQ)

2026-02-25 Marco Chen: Updated spec to prefer 'pin > region > tier > canary' as default but expose policy.override_order to advanced projects. Sending to ENG for implementation estimates.
decision_log: 2026-02-23: Decision to default to enforcing pins above tier routing but allow opt-out via policy.override_order on a per-project basis.
